title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: A year-round set of RIT’s officially identified campus traditions, from welcoming new Tigers to celebrating graduates.

cards.title: New Student Orientation
cards.subtitle: The pre-semester welcome series
cards.notes: Use the orientation schedule to meet campus resources and begin building connections before classes start; dates and activities are published by RIT.
cards.short_summary: RIT’s organized transition into campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT identifies New Student Orientation as a series of events and activities that helps students and families transition to life at RIT before classes begin.
cards.access_notes: Dates vary annually; consult RIT’s orientation schedule.

cards.title: Tiger Walk
cards.subtitle: New Tigers’ procession to convocation
cards.notes: Watch for the annual first-year procession on the Quarter Mile, where campus community members cheer as new students head to Fall Convocation.
cards.short_summary: A spirited welcome procession for incoming students.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT says the first Tiger Walk was held in 2004 and describes faculty, staff, students, and family members cheering incoming students along the Quarter Mile.
cards.access_notes: Held as part of New Student Convocation; timing is set with fall orientation.

cards.title: TigerFest
cards.subtitle: First-week celebration of a new academic year
cards.notes: Browse the first-week program for activities that connect students with fellow Tigers, campus opportunities, and RIT’s student-life traditions.
cards.short_summary: RIT’s welcome festival for the start of classes.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes TigerFest as bringing the community together during the first week of classes to celebrate the start of a new academic year.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists TigerFest for Aug. 23–29, 2026; individual events vary.

cards.title: FallFest
cards.subtitle: RIT’s autumn seasonal celebration
cards.notes: Check the annual FallFest program for fall-themed events presented by campus departments, student clubs, and student organizations.
cards.short_summary: A campus-wide marker of the Rochester fall season.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT calls FallFest the kickoff to its annual seasonal celebrations and says it includes events sponsored by departments and student clubs and organizations.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists FallFest for Sept. 17–20, 2026; consult the event program.

cards.entity_name: Brick City Homecoming and Family Weekend
cards.title: Brick City Homecoming and Family Weekend
cards.subtitle: Families, alumni, and Tigers gather on campus
cards.notes: Review the weekend schedule for campus activities, including speakers, the Brick City 5K, and Tiger athletic events.
cards.short_summary: RIT’s annual homecoming and family gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes Brick City Homecoming and Family Weekend as a yearly tradition honoring families, students, alumni, staff, and friends of the university.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists the 2026 weekend as Oct. 16–18; individual activities have separate details.

cards.title: FreezeFest
cards.subtitle: The winter tradition with Roarie the white tiger
cards.notes: Bundle up and follow the multi-day FreezeFest calendar for winter activities; RIT highlights ice skating and visits from white tiger mascot Roarie.
cards.short_summary: A winter campus celebration built around cold-weather activities.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT calls FreezeFest a longstanding annual winter tradition with multiple days of festivities, including ice skating, and identifies Roarie as its white tiger mascot.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists FreezeFest for Jan. 31–Feb. 6, 2027; check the calendar for activities.

cards.title: SpringFest
cards.subtitle: Pre-finals spring celebration
cards.notes: See the SpringFest lineup before finals for music, games, food, and other RIT-programmed activities celebrating the end of the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A springtime pause before final exams.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes SpringFest as an end-of-academic-year spring celebration before finals with music, food, games, and free swag.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists SpringFest for April 15–18, 2027; event offerings vary.

cards.title: Imagine RIT
cards.subtitle: University-wide innovation and creativity showcase
cards.notes: Plan time to explore hands-on demonstrations, interactive presentations, performances, and exhibits created by RIT students, faculty, and staff.
cards.short_summary: An annual public showcase of work made across RIT.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT says Imagine RIT is a university-wide event with hundreds of exhibits, hands-on demonstrations, interactive presentations, and performances.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists Imagine RIT for April 24, 2027; consult the event site for exhibit details.

cards.title: Commencement
cards.subtitle: RIT’s final academic celebration
cards.notes: Graduating students can follow RIT’s commencement guidance for academic convocation, college ceremonies, and Grad Week events such as Passing the Torch.
cards.short_summary: The ceremonial close of an RIT degree.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes Commencement as the final chapter at RIT, including academic convocation, college ceremonies, and Grad Week events such as Passing the Torch.
cards.access_notes: RIT lists commencement for May 7–8, 2027; eligibility and ceremony details are published separately.

cards.title: ROAR Day
cards.subtitle: RIT’s annual day of giving
cards.notes: Follow RIT’s annual giving updates to support an RIT college, program, scholarship, or activity that matters to you.
cards.evidence_claim: RIT describes ROAR Day as an annual day of giving that lets the RIT community support areas of the university that enriched their experience.
cards.source_title: Tigers flex their philanthropic muscles on ROAR Day | RIT
cards.access_notes: Participation may involve making a gift; follow RIT’s current ROAR Day announcement.
